evidence.snippet: The analbuminemic trait of the proband was caused by a homozygous AT deletion at nucleotides c. 228-229, the 91st and 92nd bases of exon 3.

evidence.snippet: The Kayseri mutation appears to be the most common cause of analbuminemia in humans, and is found in individuals belonging to geographically distant, and apparently unrelated ethnic groups.

nodes.description: Serum albumin is absent or below about 1 g/L instead of the normal 35-50 g/L. This removes the protein that normally makes up 60-65% of plasma protein, supplies about 80% of plasma oncotic pressure, and carries long-chain fatty acids, bilirubin, calcium, thyroid hormones and many drugs.

evidence.reference_title: Variations in the Human Serum Albumin Gene: Molecular and Functional Aspects.
evidence.snippet: ALB is the most abundant protein (approximately 35–50 gr/L) in plasma, representing 60–65% of total proteins, and contributes to approximately 80% of the oncotic plasma pressure [1].

nodes.description: Intravenous human albumin is used for symptomatic edema, in pregnancy (for polyhydramnios and around delivery) and before surgery. It transiently lowers cholesterol, improves endothelial function and reduces platelet activation; the effect lasts only as long as the infused albumin.

evidence.reference_title: Treatment of a patient with congenital analbuminemia with atorvastatin and albumin infusion.
evidence.snippet: Two-months of infusion with albumin improved FMD (7%) and reduced serum cholesterol (273 mg/dL), supporting the hypothesis of a compensatory role of hypercholesterolemia.

evidence.reference_title: Pregnancy in a patient with congenital analbuminaemia.
evidence.snippet: Our patient suffered from polyhydramnios during her pregnancy which was successfully managed with albumin transfusions and had a normal vaginal delivery with no complications in the intrapartum or postpartum period.

nodes.description: Engineered albumin-null mouse used to study fatty acid trafficking, glucose metabolism and the pharmacokinetics of albumin-based drugs. Like adult patients, it tolerates the absence of albumin.

nodes.description: More than 27 ALB loss-of-function variants are known, nearly all private to one family: splice-site variants, nonsense variants, frameshift deletions and insertions, and one start-codon variant. Each truncates or prevents translation of preproalbumin. Truncated products lacking the signal and propeptide are thought to be misrouted and degraded inside the hepatocyte, and some transcripts are probably removed by nonsense-mediated decay. One frameshift deletion, Kayseri (c.228_229del), accounts for about a third of known cases, which suggests a founder effect.

evidence.reference_title: Variations in the Human Serum Albumin Gene: Molecular and Functional Aspects.
evidence.snippet: In 28 other cases, the pathogenic variants (mainly affecting splicing, nonsense, and deletions), mostly in the homozygous form, cause a premature stop in the synthesis of the protein and lead to the condition known as congenital analbuminaemia.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis, Phenotype, and Molecular Genetics of Congenital Analbuminemia.
evidence.snippet: Most are unique, peculiar for each affected family, but one, a frame-shift deletion called Kayseri, has been found to cause about one third of the known cases allowing to presume a founder effect.

genetic_context.description: Usually homozygous, often in consanguineous families; compound heterozygosity is also reported.

nodes.description: The liver raises the plasma concentration of globulins (alpha-1, alpha-2 and beta fractions most consistently), transferrin, alpha-1-antitrypsin, ceruloplasmin, thyroxine-binding globulin, apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins and coagulation factors. These proteins take over part of albumin's oncotic and carrier roles, which is why adults are mildly affected. The compensation is partial: total plasma protein is still below the reference range in most patients.

nodes.description: Albumin is the main plasma carrier of long-chain fatty acids and also binds bilirubin, calcium, thyroid hormones and many drugs. In its absence apolipoprotein B-100 takes over part of fatty acid transport, serum bilirubin binding capacity falls to about a quarter of normal, and the unbound fraction of albumin-bound drugs rises. Albumin-knockout mice have lower plasma free fatty acids and less hepatic lipid. Ionized calcium is usually normal, though hypocalcemia has been described in a child.

nodes.description: Cholesterol synthesis and apolipoprotein B-containing lipoprotein output rise, producing marked hypercholesterolemia with raised LDL cholesterol and apolipoprotein B; HDL cholesterol and triglycerides are usually normal in adults. The hypercholesterolemia is generally read as part of the compensation, with lipoproteins contributing oncotic pressure and taking over some fatty acid transport, and it falls transiently when albumin is infused. In the Nagase analbuminemic rat, hepatic HMG-CoA reductase activity is increased. The phenotype resembles the lipid response to albumin loss in nephrotic syndrome.

nodes.description: Patients have increased platelet aggregation and platelet activation markers with raised oxidative stress, and in a pediatric series raised fibrinogen, D-dimer and factor XI activity. Protein C and protein S also rise, so the balance is not simply procoagulant. Albumin normally binds antithrombin and restrains platelet aggregation. Thrombotic events reported include a life-threatening cerebral thrombosis in a child and recurrent acute coronary syndrome in a young adult.

nodes.description: Without albumin, colloid osmotic pressure falls. Edema is milder than this would predict, because the rise in other plasma proteins partly restores oncotic pressure, the hydrostatic gradient from capillary to interstitium falls, and capillary protein permeability falls. Lower blood pressure is part of this adaptation. The fall is still enough to cause mild edema in adults, edema and fluid retention in infants, and it is the proposed basis of oligohydramnios and placental abnormalities before birth.

evidence.reference_title: Diagnosis, Phenotype, and Molecular Genetics of Congenital Analbuminemia.
evidence.snippet: Systemic and pronounced oedema is not seen, because oedema-preventive mechanisms are operative such as mitigation of the effect on the oncotic gradient and lowering of the hydrostatic blood pressure gradient from the capillaries to the interstitial fluids as well as a decrease in the capillary permeability of proteins (Koot et al., 2004).

evidence.snippet: The unique occurrence helps confirm earlier reports that albumin is not the exclusive factor responsible for maintaining colloid oncotic pressure.

nodes.description: Statins such as atorvastatin or simvastatin are used for the hypercholesterolemia. Because the cholesterol rise may be compensatory, lowering it has been followed by peripheral edema; combining statins with periodic albumin infusion has been proposed. Many drugs are highly albumin-bound, so free drug levels and side-effects need watching.

evidence.snippet: For example, in many cases the hypercholesterolemia has been treated with cholesterol-lowering drugs such as simvastatin or atorvastatin.
